# ASEN capability completion
Complete the approved Pi-first capability roadmap using existing ASEN mechanisms; later add presentation and client adapters without claiming unsupported equivalence.
Base branch: `feat/strict-parity-prerequisites`; current delivery: bounded work branches and reviewable PRs authorized at L474, no merge/releases; checks: focused Node/tsx tests, typecheck/build, applicable audits and isolated provider-free journeys. Older local-only delivery entries remain historical.

## Specs

### S1 — Authorized outcome and reference boundary

User authorization, verbatim: "adelante con ese plan".

The approved proposal compares the current ASEN implementation with Reference B release `v4.2.0`, target commit `4acaf4241beae1e0c977c92dfe406a270f8d40de`. The separate Reference A workspace experience is a later block, not a feature of Reference B's configuration binary. Preserve the historical frozen ecosystem source `08de420ca29be16b6f6bee725a30b599b061df16` and its evidence. A new comparison target never silently replaces that baseline or promotes a claim. L51 authorizes using installed Reference Shell 4.3.0 behavior to resolve remaining product decisions; this does not silently rebaseline the v4.2.0 comparison or establish remote-version equivalence.

### S2 — Reuse and truthful inventory

Inventory implementation, production composition, deterministic tests, real-host evidence and remaining gaps separately. Reconcile stale documentation against source. Classify each adopted surface as demonstrated, integration needed, evidence needed, missing or explicitly different. Reuse the existing routing, dispatcher, task, memory, profile and review components. The existing `ecosystem-strict-parity.md` remains the detailed ecosystem execution backlog; this document coordinates the newly approved completion program and links to those units rather than creating replacement stores or duplicating their evidence.

### S3 — Proportional workflow

Support natural-language requests, read-only inspection, focused clarification, direct small changes, durable substantial plans, task dependencies, delegation for a named reason and disjoint parallel work. Keep user requirements unchanged across handoffs. One consistent routing decision must serve the chat bridge, command materializer and agent paths. Continue already-authorized read-only work without redundant confirmation. Keep coherent code/test/doc units reviewable; task count and file count alone must not force delegation.

### S4 — Permission and identity boundaries

Preserve exact-candidate, exact-surface writer authorization; primary-session and child-process guards; sensitive-path and destructive-command protection; project/session/worktree ownership; explicit foreign-project consent; and safe cancellation. A denied call must execute zero forbidden operations. Persisted descriptions, memory and successful agent output must never restore or manufacture permission.

Approved sensitive-path policy (L16): block tool access to `.git`, `.env*`, `*.pem` and `*.key`. User correction (L21), verbatim: "dejalo como lo esa haciendo reference". For the pending shell/PowerShell and Pi-floor decisions, align with the installed Reference Shell `reference-pi` 4.3.0 behavior: Pi minimum 1.2.0 and reference normal-mode command admission rather than universal exact-effective-command confirmation. Resolve exact reference policy from authorized installed source before implementation; do not infer adoption of unrelated YOLO/Auto modes, providers, background tools or stores. Preserve sensitive-path protection and child authority. Tool-call admission remains defense in depth, not shell/OS confinement; older host tests do not prove the new minimum.

### S5 — Recovery and independent acceptance

Complete the real interrupted-writer journey using the existing ECO-06 harness, stores and inspection tools. Preserve partial edits for explicit resolution, reject automatic replay and dirty-candidate fresh-plan eligibility, create a newly bound candidate/plan and obtain fresh one-use authority before another writer. Verify identity rejection, cancellation cleanup and restart behavior. Agent completion alone never completes a linked task; independent acceptance must remain explicit. An ASEN-host kill is not independent proof of an abrupt Pi-child kill or mid-write durability.

### S6 — Tests and exact-change review

Use applicable test-first development, regressions for touched existing behavior and proportionate verification. Complete the existing review lifecycle rather than adding competing authority. Bind review to an immutable exact candidate, validate bounded corrections, invalidate stale results and disclose unavailable review. Keep review switch/consent human-owned. A review result never authorizes publication. ASEN must not acquire a mandatory external review-runtime dependency.

Candidate policy resolved by L51: support both committed commit/PR ranges and immutable local workspace snapshots, following the verified installed Reference behavior. Local snapshots use a private index/tree and owned read-only view without moving the contributor HEAD/branch/index; selected untracked scope must be explicit and current-candidate drift must invalidate results. Reuse ASEN candidate/controller/result/correction mechanisms; snapshot data is not a second approval authority. Generic Todo verification is not native review approval.

### S7 — Memory, skills and code knowledge

Keep the existing local memory implementation. Verify useful project context, search, deletion, restart continuity and project isolation without storing credentials or restoring authority. Complete skill selection/discovery/cache refresh, missing/recreated sources and real-host lifecycle coverage. Verify the unified CodeGraph tool against a real disposable project, including permitted index initialization and read-only queries. Live documentation is optional and must preserve personal configuration and disclose unavailability.

### S8 — Profiles, persona and usage

Complete effective model/effort routing, persistence, fallback and visible actual routing. Keep persona/style independent from permissions. Show only measured usage/cost and provider limits that can actually be enforced. An estimate, cancellation after quota failure or two prompts is not a hard request/token ceiling. Optional integrations and telemetry require explicit selection/consent; do not add hidden transmission.

### S9 — Installation and maintenance

User instruction, verbatim (L175): "hazlo como lo hace reference shell y completa esta parte que falta en asen". Implement the missing ASEN installation/maintenance lifecycle using the relevant logic of the already-authorized installed Reference Shell 4.3.0 reference. This supersedes the previous small-fix-only implementation boundary, not the separate execution/permission constraints in S12. Retain existing ASEN mechanisms and bind the implementation units to concrete reference behavior before writing source.

Verify clean install, home/config precedence, spaces/Unicode, declared platform support, packaged exports, optional components/presets, safe update, backup/restore, read-only diagnosis and managed-only removal. Preserve unrelated personal configuration and project data. Documentation/help/errors must follow shipped behavior. Prove restore as well as backup creation. No installer or permission-changing action is authorized merely to make a local check pass.

### S10 — Workspace experience

After the core is reliable, compose status, agents, changes, task list, private history, background command completion, bounded cross-session communication, terminal accessibility and customization from the authoritative existing state. Views must not create a second task list or grant authority. Background jobs report observed exits, never inferred success. This block is distinct from Reference B release equivalence.

### S11 — Additional clients

Keep the Pi runtime as the first validated target. Later implement explicit client adapters around shared ASEN behavior and declare each client's actual capabilities; never assume identical tools, delegation or permissions across clients. Add clients individually after a concrete mapping. Do not claim multi-client equivalence from Pi-only checks or promise every listed client the same feature set. Resolve non-Pi adapter order from concrete Reference/reference capability mapping under L51, without routine product questions; missing reference or host evidence never permits fabricated capability claims.
